REAL ESTATE BROKER'S DUTY TO NOTIFY THE DRE OF A SALESPERSON'S TERMINATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Golden State Realty Group, Inc. · Dana R. Whitfield

PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet addresses one specific, narrow legal duty that is triggered when Dana R. Whitfield's affiliation with Golden State Realty Group, Inc. as a real estate salesperson (or as a broker acting in the capacity of a salesperson) ends: the responsible broker's duty to notify the California Real Estate Commissioner of that termination. It is separate from, and does not restate, this corpus's general Real Estate Broker and Salesperson Licensing Law Information Sheet (which covers licensing requirements generally) or this corpus's general final-wage, commission-payout, and unemployment-insurance documents (which address money owed at the end of an employment relationship, not a licensing-status notice to the state's real estate regulator).

THE RESPONSIBLE BROKER'S DUTY TO NOTIFY THE COMMISSIONER OF A TERMINATION
Whenever Dana R. Whitfield's affiliation with Golden State Realty Group, Inc. is terminated, California law requires Golden State Realty Group, Inc., as the responsible broker, to provide notice of that termination to the Real Estate Commissioner. The statute does not itself spell out the notice's format, timing, or delivery method; instead, it directs the Commissioner to specify "the manner" in which that notice must be given, and Golden State Realty Group, Inc.'s notice duty is defined by reference to whatever manner the Commissioner has specified.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The commissioner shall specify the manner in which a responsible broker shall provide notice to the commissioner of an affiliation with a real estate licensee or by which a real estate licensee shall provide notice of a change of address or affiliation."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10161.8(a) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, Commissioner's authority to specify the manner of notice (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10161.8.)
  "Whenever an affiliation with a real estate licensee is terminated, the responsible broker shall provide notice to the commissioner in a manner specified by the commissioner."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10161.8(d) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, responsible broker's duty to notify the commissioner of a termination (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10161.8.)
  Known gap: This clause states Business and Professions Code section 10161.8 exactly as it reads today, current through this session's dual, independently User-Agent-varied fetch from California Legislative Information (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) on 2026-09-09; both fetches produced byte-identical statutory text. This section was substantially rewritten, effective January 1, 2019, by AB 2884 (Stats. 2018, Ch. 285, Sec. 42) — the current text no longer contains the older "immediately" and "in writing" language that some secondary summaries of this section (written before that 2019 amendment) still repeat; this clause states only the current, post-2019 text as fetched.

THE SAME SECTION ALSO REQUIRES NOTICE WHEN A BROKER RETAINS A SALESPERSON OR ANOTHER BROKER
The termination-notice duty described above is one part of a broader, two-way notice scheme within the same statutory section. The same section separately requires a responsible broker to notify the Commissioner, in the manner the Commissioner specifies, whenever that broker retains a real estate salesperson to conduct licensed activities, and requires the same notice whenever a responsible broker instead retains another real estate broker to act in the capacity of a salesperson. In practice, this means that if Dana R. Whitfield goes on to affiliate with a new responsible broker after leaving Golden State Realty Group, Inc., that new broker independently owes the Commissioner its own notice of that new affiliation — a separate notice from, and not a substitute for, Golden State Realty Group, Inc.'s own notice of the termination described above.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Whenever a responsible broker retains a real estate salesperson to conduct activities requiring a license, the responsible broker shall notify the commissioner in a manner specified by the commissioner."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10161.8(b) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, notice duty when retaining a salesperson (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10161.8.)
  "Whenever a responsible broker retains a real estate broker to conduct activities requiring a license, the responsible broker shall provide notice to the commissioner in a manner specified by the commissioner."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10161.8(c) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, notice duty when retaining another broker as a salesperson (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10161.8.)
  Known gap: Both citations below are subdivisions (b) and (c) of the same statutory section already quoted above (Bus. & Prof. Code § 10161.8), fetched in the same dual, User-Agent-varied session as the termination-notice clause above; they are not independent of that clause's source, though they address a distinct notice trigger (retaining a licensee, rather than terminating an affiliation with one).

THE IMPLEMENTING REGULATION'S TEN-DAY MAILING DEADLINE FOR A BROKER-TO-BROKER TERMINATION
A Real Estate Commissioner regulation implementing the statute above supplies one of the specific timing details the statute itself leaves to the Commissioner to specify, for the particular case of a responsible broker terminating a contract retaining another broker to act as a salesperson: that regulation requires the responsible broker to give notice of the termination by mailing it to the Commissioner not more than ten days after the termination. The same regulation also describes a retention-notice form used when a broker newly retains a salesperson or another broker, and states that this form may, as an acceptable alternative, be used by a departing salesperson's predecessor broker to give the predecessor's own notice of the termination of that prior relationship.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "A responsible broker that is involved in a contract to retain another broker to act in the capacity of a salesperson must give notice of the termination of that broker/broker contract relationship as required by Section 10161.8(b) of the Business and Professions Code by mailing such notice to the Commissioner not more than ten days following such termination."
  — Cal. Code Regs. tit. 10, § 2752(b) (Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute, text of the California Code of Regulations), California Code of Regulations, Title 10 (Real Estate Commissioner), notice deadline for termination of a broker-to-broker retention contract (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/10-CCR-2752)
  "As an acceptable alternative to (5) and (6) above, the form may be utilized by the predecessor responsible broker to give notice of the termination of the broker/salesperson contract relationship as required by Section 10161.8(b) of the Business and Professions Code if this notice is mailed to the Commissioner not more than ten days following such termination."
  — Cal. Code Regs. tit. 10, § 2752(a) (Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute, text of the California Code of Regulations), California Code of Regulations, Title 10 (Real Estate Commissioner), alternative use of the retention-notice form to report a predecessor termination (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/10-CCR-2752)
  Known gap: This clause is drawn from Title 10, California Code of Regulations, section 2752, as published by Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute (a regulatory-text mirror already relied on elsewhere in this corpus for federal Code of Federal Regulations text, e.g. this corpus's existing WARN Act Layoff Notice document's citation to 20 C.F.R. § 639.9(c)); this session fetched that page twice, with two distinct User-Agent strings, and the two fetches were textually identical. This regulation's own text internally cites "Section 10161.8(b) of the Business and Professions Code" for the broker-to-broker termination-notice duty described above and, separately, for a salesperson's certification duty referenced in the same regulation, it cites "Section 10161.8(d)." Neither cross-reference matches the current lettering of section 10161.8 fetched for the two clauses above, where subdivision (b) concerns retaining a salesperson (not terminating one) and subdivision (d) concerns the broker's own termination-notice duty (not a salesperson's certification duty). The regulation's own "Notes" state it was last amended effective April 1, 2022 — after section 10161.8's January 1, 2019 renumbering — so this appears to be an uncorrected internal cross-reference carried forward through that later regulatory amendment, not a difference in which version of the statute is in effect. This clause states the regulation's ten-day mailing deadline and alternative-form provision as written, without resolving that internal cross-reference discrepancy or assuming which current subdivision the regulation's drafters meant.

A SALESPERSON CANNOT BE COMPENSATED FOR LICENSED ACTIVITY OUTSIDE THE CURRENT BROKER RELATIONSHIP
Separately from the Commissioner-notice duty described above, California law restricts who may pay, and who may receive, compensation for activity that requires a real estate license. A real estate salesperson may not accept compensation for that kind of activity from anyone other than the broker under whom the salesperson is licensed at the time; a broker who compensates a person for that kind of activity is limited to a licensed real estate broker or a real estate salesperson licensed under that same responsible broker; and a licensed real estate salesperson may not pay compensation to another licensee for that kind of activity except through the broker under whom the salesperson is licensed at the time (though two licensees may agree to share compensation paid through the responsible broker). A violation of these restrictions exposes the license of the real estate licensee involved to temporary suspension or permanent revocation by the Commissioner, following a hearing.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "It is unlawful for any licensed real estate broker to retain, compensate, directly or indirectly, any person for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter who is not a licensed real estate broker, or a real estate salesperson licensed under the responsible broker retaining or compensating him or her"
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10137, first paragraph (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, restriction on a broker's compensation of unlicensed persons or non-affiliated licensees (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10137.)
  "No real estate salesperson shall accept compensation for activity requiring a real estate license from any person other than the broker under whom he or she is at the time licensed."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10137, second paragraph (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, restriction on a salesperson accepting compensation outside the current broker relationship (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10137.)
  "For a violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the real estate licensee, in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 10137, fourth paragraph (California Legislative Information, official text), California Business and Professions Code, Real Estate Law, license suspension or revocation for a violation of this section (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=10137.)
  Known gap: This clause states Business and Professions Code section 10137 as it reads today, confirmed via a dual, User-Agent-varied fetch from California Legislative Information on 2026-09-09 that produced byte-identical text both times. This clause states the statute's general restriction on who may pay and receive compensation for licensed real estate activity; it does not independently determine how this restriction interacts with any specific commission owed to a departing salesperson for a transaction pending or completed before termination, which depends on facts (such as the timing and terms of any commission-sharing or referral agreement) not addressed here.

Salesperson: Dana R. Whitfield
